testCases.name: test_case_0
testCases.input: what is vibe testing and why isn't it enough for deploying an llm app?
testCases.actualOutput:
Vibe testing is exactly what it sounds like — you casually try out your LLM application with a handful of prompts, maybe five or ten questions that come to mind in the moment, and then judge whether it's "working" based on a gut feeling. You read the responses, they seem right, and you move on. The term captures that informal, subjective approach: there's no fixed test suite, no consistent criteria, and no documentation of what you checked.

The reason it falls short for production deployment is that it's fundamentally not repeatable. The questions you think to ask today won't be the same ones you ask next week, and they certainly won't cover the edge cases your real users will encounter. Because it's based on feel rather than measurable criteria, you can't reliably compare versions, track regressions, or give stakeholders confidence that the system behaves consistently. The course material emphasizes that while vibe testing might be fine for a personal project, teams that have relied on it for production LLM applications have run into serious problems — essentially shipping software that hasn't been properly validated.
